instructions: A friendly woman from Edinburgh speaking gentle, conversational Scottish English. A light, natural everyday Scottish accent, relaxed and understated. Calm, warm and reassuring, like speaking one-to-one with a five-year-old. Use an unhurried, clear pace and small pauses. Keep the delivery soft and matter-of-fact, without theatrical emphasis, a sing-song teaching voice, or exaggerated R sounds. Pronounce Zach as Zak. Read only the supplied words exactly. No music, sound effects or extra words.

hello.text: Hi Zach! Let’s make some music. Tap the Let's play button.

stop.text: Hear that beat? Watch the light move along. When it goes back to the start, the tune plays again. Tap Stop.

drum.text: Tap this drum. Give it a go!

beat.text: Tap this box. A lit box makes a beat. A dark box is a rest.

tunes.text: Let’s make a tune. Tap Tunes.

note.text: Tap this box. Notes at the top sound high. Notes at the base sound low.

chord.text: Add one more note in the same stack. They play at once. That is a chord!

sounds.text: Try a new sound. Tap Sounds.

slide.text: Slide this. The shape and the sound change. Try soft, then bright.

play.text: Now hear your tune. Tap the Let's play button.

done.text: You made music! Have fun, Zach.

reward-drum.text: Your drum! That was you. Tap Next.

reward-beat.text: Your beat! That was you. Tap Next.

reward-note.text: Your note! That was you. Tap Next.

reward-chord.text: Your notes! That was you. Tap Next.

reward-slide.text: Your sound! That was you. Tap Next.
